transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: David Lopez, Priya Menon, Ethan Zhang (Redwood); Maya Patel, Jordan Reed, Liam O'Sullivan, Sofia Ramos (Aperture Health)

00:00 - David Lopez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is David from Redwood, i'm the account exec on the engagement, with me is Priya our CSM and Ethan who's our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:18 - Maya Patel: Good, thanks. Excited to get started. Hi all.
00:25 - Jordan Reed: Hey, yep, thanks. We've been waiting for this, we'll go through security and infra and then the pilot.
00:36 - David Lopez: Great. Quick agenda. we want to align on success criteria for the pilot, confirm what environment you'll use — hosted vs dedicated vs private — surface any security blockers, and walk through next steps and timeline. Does that sound right?
00:50 - Sofia Ramos: Yep, that works. Also want to confirm who's owning what from our side.
01:02 - Priya Menon: I'll be the CSM leading onboarding, point of contact for the runbook and weekly syncs. I'll follow up with a detailed timeline after this call.
01:12 - Ethan Zhang: I'll handle the technical provisioning and integrations, bench numbers, and will run the initial load tests.
01:22 - Liam O'Sullivan: On our side, i'll be implementing infra changes, coordinating with security, and electric... I mean, our infra team.
01:30 - David Lopez: Okay, first, success criteria. Maya, what are you trying to validate in the pilot?
01:42 - Maya Patel: Primary things: model latency under typical QPS, cost per 1k tokens, and end-to-end data privacy — we can't send PHI to 3rd-party without controls. We'll also track prediction quality vs our internal baseline.
01:58 - Ethan Zhang: When you say PHI, are you looking for VPC/on-prem or is encrypted-hosted with KMS acceptable?
02:07 - Maya Patel: We prefer customer-managed keys and VPC peering for the pilot if possible, but we can consider hosted with strict data retention and KMS if the compliance team signs off.
02:20 - Jordan Reed: Also SOC 2 attestation is non-negotiable, and SSO via SAML/Okta is required.
02:30 - Priya Menon: Redwood has SOC 2 and SSO integrations, and we offer private deployment for stricter needs. I'll share the SOC 2 report and our SSO docs after this call.
02:44 - David Lopez: To clarify options: 1) Hosted API — fastest, lower ops overhead; 2) Dedicated — reserved GPU cluster (isolated) offering predictable throughput; 3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full control for regulated data. For the pilot most customers start with Dedicated in a customer-isolated VPC or Hosted with customer-managed KMS.
03:06 - Liam O'Sullivan: For performance testing, we'll want KV cache behavior documented — we use long context windows for some workflows. What's the typical cache hit rate strategy?
03:18 - Ethan Zhang: Good question. Our runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching; hit rate depends on prompt overlap. For the pilot we can enable prefix caching and run a couple of synthetic workloads to estimate cost and latency.
03:31 - Maya Patel: Great. On timeline: we want a 4-week pilot, then decide on production rollout. Is that feasible?
03:41 - David Lopez: Absolutely feasible. Typical pilot schedule: week 1 provisioning and smoke tests, week 2 integration and sample workloads, week 3 load testing and quality evals, week 4 optimization (batching, quantization suggestions) and final review.
03:58 - Jordan Reed: For provisioning, network terms: do you require inbound firewall rules to our infra? We prefer to minimize inbound from external services.
04:08 - Ethan Zhang: For dedicated in our cloud, you'll provision a peered VPC and we'll deploy in it; minimal inbound is required. For hosted, it's outbound to Redwood endpoints only, no peering but we'd need KMS access if you use customer-managed keys.
04:25 - Sofia Ramos: Do you support IP allowlists for the hosted API?
04:30 - Priya Menon: Yes, IP allowlists and IP-restricted API keys are supported. I'll include docs.
04:39 - Maya Patel: On security questionnaire, can you walk through encryption at rest and in transit?
04:44 - David Lopez: Sure. In transit TLS 1.2+, at rest encrypted via AES-256 managed keys; for customer-managed keys we integrate with KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK). For private on-prem we hand off the keys to the customer's HSM if needed.
05:06 - Jordan Reed: Is audit logging available for all requests? We need per-request logs for compliance.
05:12 - Ethan Zhang: Yes, audit logs with request id, user id, and model variant are available. Retention periods are configurable; we'll surface the defaults and options in the runbook.
05:25 - Maya Patel: About data retention: we need logs for 7 years for some records — is that supported?
05:32 - Priya Menon: We can configure long-term retention via the enterprise add-on; i'll note that and include pricing details.
05:41 - Liam O'Sullivan: Let's talk about costs. Do you have a cost model for dedicated? We need per-token and per-hour GPU burn rates to evaluate TCO.
05:51 - David Lopez: For dedicated we provide committed monthly capacity and per-instance burn rates; we'll share a pilot cost estimate based on the traffic profile you provide. For hosted, it's usage-based per token. We'll send a sample cost sheet.
06:07 - Maya Patel: We'll send an expected QPS and token distributions — typical messages are 128-512 tokens. Some long reports hit 2k tokens occasionally.
06:20 - Ethan Zhang: That's helpful. Long sequences may change kernel selection and latency; we'll configure model variants and quantization profiles accordingly.
06:29 - Jordan Reed: Any limitations around custom models or fine-tuning? We might want to bring our own fine-tuned model later.
06:36 - Ethan Zhang: We support customer model uploads in Dedicated/Private; hosted can support model hosting via our managed model registry depending on licensing. We'll document the onboarding steps for custom models.
06:48 - Maya Patel: For the pilot, we want Redwood to run bench tests against a representative subset of queries and share the latency distribution and 95th percentile.
06:57 - David Lopez: We'll do that. Ethan will run baseline load tests and provide p50/p95/p99 latency and TPS metrics.
07:06 - Ethan Zhang: I'll also include token breakdown and CPU/GPU utilization graphs. Might be slight misspell in our tools export sometimes.
07:14 - Sofia Ramos: How will we handle incident response during the pilot? We need an escalation path.
07:20 - Priya Menon: Priya here. We'll share the support SLAs and a dedicated onboarding channel. For critical incidents you'll have a phone and pager contact for the engineering lead.
07:31 - Jordan Reed: Excellent. On privacy, we need to avoid sending raw PHI to third parties. Are there transformations or redaction options?
07:40 - Ethan Zhang: We can set up pre-processing hooks or operate inside your VPC so data never leaves your environment. For hosted we can also set up an edge transformation layer. We'll include patterns in the runbook.
07:55 - Maya Patel: For the pilot, we prefer dedicated with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS if possible.
08:04 - David Lopez: Noted. We'll mark pilot baseline as Dedicated + VPC + CMK.
08:11 - Liam O'Sullivan: Regarding networking, we'll need a set of IPs from Redwood and an ARN for KMS access.
08:18 - Ethan Zhang: I'll provide the IP ranges and KMS integration steps.
08:24 - Maya Patel: Next, who will run the validation tests? We'll do joint validation — your SE to run baseline, we'll run integration tests.
08:33 - Ethan Zhang: Agreed. We'll provide test scripts and examples. We'll also provide a small benchmark harness you can run locally to replicate results.
08:44 - David Lopez: Any regulatory constraints we should be aware of? data residency?
08:48 - Jordan Reed: We must keep data in US regions only for this pilot; production might require EU for European customers.
08:56 - Priya Menon: We have region controls. We'll note US-only for pilot.
09:02 - Sofia Ramos: Ok timeline recap?
09:06 - David Lopez: Week 0 (this week): finalize runbook and provisioning plan. Week 1: provisioning + smoke tests. Week 2: integration + initial evals. Week 3: load tests and optimization. Week 4: review and decision.
09:22 - Maya Patel: Works for us.
09:25 - Jordan Reed: A few clarifying Qs — do you provide per-route rate limiting and token-level cost visibility?
09:33 - Ethan Zhang: Yes, the Console has per-route token breakdowns and latency dashboards. We'll share screenshots in the runbook.
09:41 - David Lopez: Any concerns about fallback if capacity is impacted? We have automated fallback policies to other model variants or regions. We can discuss warm standby models for critical flows.
09:53 - Liam O'Sullivan: We'll want to test fallback and retry semantics.
09:57 - Ethan Zhang: We'll include test cases for fallback and circuit-breaker behavior during load tests.
10:06 - Maya Patel: What's the onboarding support model? Do we get a dedicated TAM during the pilot?
10:11 - Priya Menon: For pilots we generally include CSM + SE support; TAMs are part of enterprise packages but we can provide an elevated support path if needed.
10:22 - Sofia Ramos: Great. Any blockers now?
10:25 - Maya Patel: Only outstanding is receiving the SOC 2 docs and runbook plus the IP/KMS details.
10:33 - David Lopez: Action: Priya will send runbook and SOC 2 link by Friday 2025-07-18. Ethan to provision dedicated pilot and share network and access info by 2025-07-22. Maya to send traffic profile and security contact by 2025-07-20.
10:54 - Jordan Reed: Sounds good. We'll review the runbook and get back with any questions.
11:03 - David Lopez: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule the weekly sync for 2025-07-23 same time.
11:10 - Maya Patel: Thanks all. Looking forward.
11:15 - Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript is moderately noisy; auto-transcription sometimes mislabels words like "KV cache" -> "K V cache" or drops punctuation. Action items and next steps summarized above.
